served: deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses
gait with a distracting or automatic task (dancing, counting backwards)
results: 1. deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal reflexes, FLEXOR plantar responses, no clonus
2. tandem gait: better than free walking
3. walking backward: the scissoring DISAPPEARS on walking backward; in spasticity it persists
4. gait with a distracting or automatic task (dancing, counting backwards): the pattern changes or normalises
5. muscle tone (spasticity, rigidity, paratonia): normal tone on passive movement despite the scissoring gait
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Functional (psychogenic) gait disorder, manifesting as a scissoring gait without underlying neurological signs

1. Frontal lobe gait disorder (gait apraxia) – can also improve with distraction, but usually accompanied by frontal cognitive signs and magnetic/shuffling rather than scissoring gait
2. Spastic paraparesis from a covert structural spinal cord lesion – made unlikely by normal tone, normal reflexes, and flexor plantars
3. Conversion disorder (now subsumed under functional neurological symptom disorder) – essentially the same entity, retained as an alternative label
